devdoc.author: Venus
devdoc.details: Stork stores the update time in nanoseconds. The ChainlinkOracle compares `updatedAt` with `block.timestamp`,      so it is reported here in seconds; in nanoseconds every read reverts with "updatedAt exceeds block time".      The value is read through Stork's own age check, which reverts once the value is older than Stork's      `validTimePeriodSeconds` (1 hour on BNB Chain). An hourly feed can pass that age shortly before a push lands,      and every price read reverts until it does. A `maxStalePeriod` on the ChainlinkOracle only binds when it is      set below Stork's limit.

returns._0: Always 18, since Stork stores every value with 18 decimals

latestRoundData().details: Stork keeps no rounds, so `roundId` and `answeredInRound` carry the update time as well.

returns.answeredInRound: Update time of the value, in seconds
returns.roundId: Update time of the value, in seconds
returns.startedAt: Update time of the value, in seconds
returns.updatedAt: Update time of the value, in seconds
